questions.q: Data collected by an investigator for the first time, for a specific purpose, are called ______ data.
questions.e: Primary data are first-hand data; secondary data are already collected by someone else and used again.

questions.q: The Census of India is conducted once every ______ years.
questions.e: The Census of India is a decennial survey, held every ten years by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner.

questions.q: A survey that collects information from every element of the population is a census or complete ______.
questions.e: A census survey covers every unit of the population, unlike a sample survey which covers only a part.

questions.q: The difference between the value of a sample statistic and the actual value of the population parameter is called ______ error.
questions.e: Sampling error arises because only a part of the population is observed; it can be reduced by taking a larger sample.

questions.q: The value that occurs most frequently in a series is called the ______.
questions.e: The mode is the most frequently occurring value in a distribution.

questions.q: Find the arithmetic mean of 12, 15, 18, 21 and 24.
questions.e: Sum = 90 and number of items = 5, so mean = 90 ÷ 5 = 18.

questions.q: Find the median of 7, 3, 9, 5, 11 and 13.
questions.e: Arranged: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. With 6 items, median = average of 3rd and 4th items = (7 + 9) ÷ 2 = 8.

questions.q: The mean marks of 30 students of Section A are 40 and the mean marks of 20 students of Section B are 50. Find the combined mean marks of all 50 students.
The mean of 5 observations is 20. If the observation 30 is removed, what is the mean of the remaining observations?
questions.e: Total = 5 × 20 = 100; after removing 30 the total is 70 for 4 items, so mean = 70 ÷ 4 = 17.5.

questions.q: The daily wages (in ₹) of 7 workers in a Ludhiana factory are: 300, 350, 400, 400, 450, 500, 750.
p: (a) Find the arithmetic mean wage in ₹.
(b) Find the median wage in ₹.
(c) Find the modal wage in ₹.
questions.e: Sum = 3150, so mean = 3150 ÷ 7 = 450; the 4th item (median) is 400; 400 occurs twice, so mode = 400. The extreme value 750 pulls the mean above the median.

questions.q: The value of the coefficient of correlation always lies between ______ and +1.
questions.e: r lies between −1 (perfect negative) and +1 (perfect positive); r = 0 means no linear correlation.

questions.q: When two variables move in the same direction, the correlation between them is ______.
questions.e: In positive correlation, an increase in one variable is associated with an increase in the other, e.g., income and expenditure.

questions.q: A diagram that plots pairs of values of two variables as points to show the nature of their relationship is a ______.
questions.e: A scatter diagram gives a visual idea of the direction and closeness of correlation without calculation.

questions.q: During a Delhi summer, as temperature rises, the sale of woollen clothes falls. The correlation between temperature and the sale of woollens is ______.
questions.e: When variables move in opposite directions, the correlation is negative.

questions.q: Two judges rank 5 contestants in a rangoli competition. Judge A's ranks: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Judge B's ranks: 2, 1, 4, 3, 5.
p: (a) Find the sum of squared differences in ranks (Σd²).
(b) Find Spearman's rank correlation coefficient.
(c) Is the correlation positive or negative?
positive|high positive|positive correlation
questions.e: d = −1, 1, −1, 1, 0 so Σd² = 4; rs = 1 − 6Σd² / (n³ − n) = 1 − 24/120 = 0.8, a high positive correlation.

questions.q: The index number for the base year is always taken as ______.
questions.e: The base year is the reference period, and its index is set at 100.

questions.q: The index number that measures changes in the general price level of goods traded in bulk in India is the ______ index.
questions.e: The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) measures changes in prices of goods at the wholesale level.

questions.q: The total price of a basket of goods was ₹200 in the base year and ₹250 in the current year. Find the simple aggregative price index.
questions.e: Index = (Σp1 ÷ Σp0) × 100 = (250 ÷ 200) × 100 = 125, showing a 25% rise in prices.

questions.q: The Consumer Price Index rose from 200 to 210 in a year. What is the rate of inflation (in %)?
Commodity A: base price ₹10, base quantity 10, current price ₹12. Commodity B: base price ₹20, base quantity 5, current price ₹24.
p: (a) Find Σp0q0.
(b) Find Σp1q0.
(c) Find Laspeyres' price index.

questions.q: In which year was India's First Five Year Plan launched?
questions.e: The First Five Year Plan covered 1951–56 and gave priority to agriculture.

questions.q: The large increase in foodgrain production in the late 1960s due to high yielding variety seeds, fertilisers and irrigation is called the ______ Revolution.
questions.e: The Green Revolution, mainly in wheat and rice, helped India achieve self-sufficiency in foodgrains.

questions.q: Which Industrial Policy Resolution formed the basis of the Second Five Year Plan? Give the year.
questions.e: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 classified industries into three categories and gave the state a leading role.

questions.q: Abolition of intermediaries like zamindars and fixing land ceilings were land reforms aimed mainly at which goal of planning?
questions.e: Land reforms tried to redistribute land to the tiller, promoting equity in the agricultural sector.

questions.q: From 1950 to 1990, India followed an inward-looking trade strategy to protect domestic industry from foreign competition.
p: (a) The strategy of producing goods at home instead of importing them is called import ______.
substitution
(b) Taxes imposed on imported goods are called ______.
tariffs|tariff|import duty|import duties|customs duty
(c) Fixing the maximum quantity of a good that can be imported is called a ______.
quota|quotas|import quota
questions.e: Import substitution protected domestic industries through tariffs, which make imports costlier, and quotas, which limit import quantities.

questions.q: In which year did India announce the New Economic Policy of liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation?
questions.e: The 1991 reforms were introduced in response to a balance of payments and fiscal crisis.

questions.q: Selling a part of the equity of public sector enterprises to the public is called ______.
questions.e: Disinvestment is a form of privatisation in which the government reduces its shareholding in PSUs.

questions.q: The organisation that succeeded GATT in 1995 to establish a rule-based world trading system is the ______.
questions.e: The WTO administers multilateral trade agreements and aims to give all countries equal opportunity in world trade.

questions.q: A US bank hires a call-centre company in Gurugram to handle its customer service. For the US bank, this is an example of ______.
questions.e: Outsourcing, boosted by globalisation and cheap communication, means a firm hires regular services from external sources, often abroad.

questions.q: Along with education, expenditure on ______ is a major source of human capital formation.
questions.e: Health spending makes people more productive, so it is a key source of human capital along with education.

questions.q: A machine can be sold separately from its owner, but a doctor's skills cannot. Physical capital is tangible, whereas human capital is ______.
questions.e: Human capital is intangible and embodied in its owner; only its services are sold, not the capital itself.

questions.q: Meena of a village in Bihar completes a nursing degree from a university, moves to Delhi for a better-paid hospital job, and is then trained by the hospital to use new equipment.
p: (a) Moving to Delhi for a better job is which source of human capital formation?
migration
(b) Being trained by the hospital at the workplace is called ______ training.
on-the-job|on the job|on-job|on job
(c) Which body regulates and funds university education in India?
ugc|university grants commission
questions.e: Migration, on-the-job training and education are all sources of human capital; the UGC coordinates and funds higher education.

questions.q: Self-help groups (SHGs) mainly help rural poor by providing small loans, known as ______.
questions.e: SHGs pool small savings and lend to members, bringing the poor into the formal credit system through microcredit.

questions.q: The apex body set up in 1982 to coordinate the activities of all institutions in the rural financing system is ______.
questions.a: nabard|national bank for agriculture and rural development
questions.e: NABARD coordinates rural credit given by cooperatives, commercial banks and regional rural banks.

questions.q: Farming that uses organic manure and bio-pesticides instead of chemical fertilisers and pesticides is called ______ farming.
questions.e: Organic farming restores and maintains ecological balance and produces chemical-free food.

questions.q: Lakshmi, a farmer in Andhra Pradesh, supplements her crop income by rearing cows, goats and poultry. This diversification into a non-crop activity is called ______.
questions.e: Animal husbandry (livestock) provides income stability, food security and employment to rural families.

questions.q: Farmers of a village in Gujarat sell milk to a cooperative dairy, sell grain in a regulated market, and borrow from a bank set up in 1975 especially for rural areas.
p: (a) Operation Flood, which built such dairy cooperatives, is associated with which revolution?
white|white revolution
(b) Collection, storage, processing and sale of farm produce is called agricultural ______.
marketing
(c) Name the banks set up in 1975 to provide credit to the rural poor.
regional rural banks|regional rural bank|rrb|rrbs
questions.e: Operation Flood led to the White Revolution; agricultural marketing gets farmers fair prices; Regional Rural Banks extend institutional credit to rural areas.

questions.q: Workers who own and operate an enterprise to earn their livelihood, like a shopkeeper, are called ______ workers.
questions.e: Self-employed workers use their own resources to earn a living; they form the largest group of workers in India.

questions.q: When more people are working on a family farm than needed, so that their marginal product is zero, the unemployment is called ______ unemployment.
questions.e: In disguised unemployment, removing some workers does not reduce total output.

questions.q: In a village, the labour force is 400 persons, of whom 340 are employed. What is the unemployment rate (in %)?
questions.e: Unemployed = 400 − 340 = 60; unemployment rate = 60 ÷ 400 × 100 = 15%.

questions.q: The population of a town is 2,00,000 and the number of workers is 76,000. Find the worker-population ratio (in %).
questions.e: Worker-population ratio = 76,000 ÷ 2,00,000 × 100 = 38%.

questions.q: In a survey in Nashik, Ramu works on his own farm, Sita works as a daily-wage labourer on construction sites, and Rahul works in a bank with provident fund and pension benefits.
p: (a) Sita is which type of worker?
casual|casual worker|casual wage labourer|casual labourer|casual wage labour
(b) Rahul is which type of worker?
regular|regular salaried|regular salaried employee|regular employee
(c) Rahul's job is in which sector: formal or informal?
formal|organised|organized
questions.e: Casual workers are hired on a daily basis without security; regular salaried employees get regular wages and social security, which is typical of the formal sector.

questions.q: The ability of the environment to absorb degradation is called its ______ capacity.
questions.e: When pollution exceeds the absorptive capacity, the environment is damaged.

questions.q: Development that meets the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs is called ______ development.
questions.e: This is the Brundtland Commission's definition of sustainable development.

questions.q: Solar energy, wind power and biogas are examples of ______ sources of energy.
questions.e: Non-conventional sources are renewable and cause little pollution, so they support sustainable development.

questions.q: When the rate of resource extraction exceeds the rate of their regeneration and pollution exceeds absorptive capacity, the environment fails to sustain life. This situation is called an environmental ______.
questions.e: Environmental crisis arises when demand on the environment is greater than its supply of resources and absorptive capacity.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: In which year did China introduce economic reforms?
questions.e: China began reforms in 1978, India in 1991 and Pakistan in 1988.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: The campaign launched in China in 1958 to industrialise rapidly, including setting up backyard furnaces, was the ______.
questions.a: great leap forward|glf|great leap forward campaign
questions.e: The Great Leap Forward aimed at rapid industrialisation, with people encouraged to set up industries in their backyards.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: Which country among India, China and Pakistan set up Special Economic Zones in 1980, soon after starting its reforms, to attract foreign investors?
questions.e: China set up its first Special Economic Zones in 1980 to attract foreign investment, which boosted its exports and growth; India's SEZ policy came only in 2000.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: This country began economic reforms in 1988. Its growth slowed in the 1990s, partly due to political instability, dependence on remittances and foreign aid, and a weak manufacturing base. Name the country.
questions.e: Pakistan's reforms began in 1988, but political instability and over-dependence on remittances and foreign aid hurt its growth.

questions.q: Goods bought by one producer from another for resale or for use as raw material during the same year are called ______ goods.
questions.e: Intermediate goods are used up in production during the year; only final goods are counted in national income to avoid double counting.

questions.q: GDP at market price is ₹1,000 crore, depreciation is ₹100 crore, net factor income from abroad is −₹20 crore and net indirect taxes are ₹80 crore. Find NNP at factor cost (in ₹ crore).
questions.e: NNPfc = GDPmp − depreciation + NFIA − NIT = 1000 − 100 − 20 − 80 = ₹800 crore.

questions.q: A firm sells output worth ₹500, its stock rises by ₹50 and it uses intermediate goods worth ₹300. Find its gross value added (in ₹).
questions.e: Value of output = sales + change in stock = 500 + 50 = 550; GVA = 550 − 300 = ₹250.

questions.q: Nominal GDP of a country is ₹1,200 crore and real GDP is ₹1,000 crore. Find the GDP deflator.
questions.e: GDP deflator = nominal GDP ÷ real GDP × 100 = 1200 ÷ 1000 × 100 = 120, meaning prices have risen 20% over the base year.

questions.q: Data (₹ crore): compensation of employees 600, rent 100, interest 80, profit 220, mixed income of self-employed 200, net factor income from abroad −30, depreciation 50, net indirect taxes 70.
p: (a) Find NDP at factor cost (₹ crore).
(b) Find national income (NNP at factor cost, ₹ crore).
(c) Find GDP at market price (₹ crore).

questions.q: The central bank of India is the ______.
questions.e: The RBI issues currency, is the banker to the government and to banks, and controls credit.

questions.q: When money is used as a common measure in which the values of all goods and services are expressed, it serves as a ______ of account.
questions.e: As a unit of account, money measures value, so prices of all goods can be compared.

questions.q: The rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities is the ______ rate.
questions.e: Under repo, banks borrow from the RBI by selling securities with an agreement to repurchase them later.

questions.q: To control inflation, the RBI should ______ the repo rate.
questions.e: A higher repo rate makes borrowing costlier for banks, reducing credit and aggregate demand, which checks inflation.

questions.q: The legal reserve ratio is 20% and a new deposit of ₹1,000 is made in the banking system. What is the total amount of deposits that can be created (in ₹)?
questions.e: Money multiplier = 1 ÷ LRR = 1 ÷ 0.2 = 5; total deposits = 1000 × 5 = ₹5,000.

questions.q: The ratio of change in consumption to change in income is called the ______.
questions.e: MPC = ΔC ÷ ΔY; it lies between 0 and 1.

questions.q: If the marginal propensity to consume is 0.9, what is the value of the investment multiplier?
When aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply at the full employment level of output, the excess is called the ______ gap.
questions.e: Excess demand at full employment cannot raise output, so it raises the price level, creating an inflationary gap.

questions.q: The marginal propensity to save is 0.25 and investment rises by ₹200 crore. By how much will income increase (in ₹ crore)?
In an economy, C = 100 + 0.75Y and investment I = 50 (₹ crore). Find the equilibrium level of income (in ₹ crore).
When national income rises from ₹4,000 crore to ₹5,000 crore, consumption rises from ₹3,500 crore to ₹4,300 crore.
p: (a) Find the MPC.
(b) Find the MPS.
(c) Find the APC at the income of ₹5,000 crore.

questions.q: A tax whose burden falls on the person on whom it is imposed and cannot be shifted to others, like income tax, is a ______ tax.
questions.e: Direct taxes like income tax and corporation tax are paid by the person on whom they are levied.

questions.q: The government sells part of its shares in a public sector company. The money it receives is a ______ receipt.
questions.e: Disinvestment reduces the government's assets, so its proceeds are non-debt capital receipts.

questions.q: The excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings is called the ______ deficit.
questions.e: Fiscal deficit shows the total borrowing requirement of the government.

questions.q: Interest paid by the government on its past borrowings is ______ expenditure.
questions.e: Interest payments neither create assets nor reduce liabilities, so they are revenue expenditure.

questions.q: The government spends money to build a new national highway. This spending is ______ expenditure.
questions.e: Spending that creates a physical asset, like a highway, is capital expenditure.

questions.q: Budget data (₹ crore): revenue receipts 1,000, revenue expenditure 1,200, capital expenditure 500, non-debt capital receipts 100, interest payments 150.
p: (a) Find the revenue deficit (₹ crore).
(b) Find the fiscal deficit (₹ crore).
(c) Find the primary deficit (₹ crore).

questions.q: The systematic record of all economic transactions of the residents of a country with the rest of the world in a year is the balance of ______.
questions.e: The balance of payments has two main accounts: the current account and the capital account.

questions.q: An exchange rate determined by the market forces of demand for and supply of foreign exchange is a ______ exchange rate.
questions.e: Under a flexible (floating) system, the exchange rate settles where demand for foreign exchange equals its supply.

questions.q: Under a flexible exchange rate, the price of one US dollar rises from ₹80 to ₹84. The Indian rupee has ______.
questions.e: When more rupees are needed to buy a dollar in a flexible system, the rupee depreciates; devaluation applies to a fixed exchange rate.

questions.q: Data for a country (₹ crore): exports of goods 500, imports of goods 700, net invisibles +150.
p: (a) Find the balance of trade (₹ crore).
(b) Find the current account balance (₹ crore).
(c) Is the current account in surplus or deficit?
deficit
questions.e: BoT = 500 − 700 = −200 (deficit); current account balance = −200 + 150 = −50, a current account deficit.

questions.q: The central problems of an economy arise mainly because of the ______ of resources.
questions.e: Resources are scarce and have alternative uses, so every economy must decide what, how and for whom to produce.

questions.q: The slope of the production possibility curve is called the marginal rate of ______.
questions.e: MRT shows how many units of one good must be given up to produce one more unit of the other.

questions.q: An economy can produce (Y, X) combinations of (0, 100), (1, 95) and (2, 85). How many units of X must be given up to produce the second unit of Y?
questions.e: Moving from (1, 95) to (2, 85), X falls by 10 units; the rising opportunity cost gives the PPC its concave shape.

questions.q: The want-satisfying power of a commodity is called ______.
questions.e: Utility is the satisfaction a consumer gets from consuming a good.

questions.q: A good whose demand falls when the consumer's income rises is called an ______ good.
questions.e: For inferior goods like coarse cereals, demand moves in the opposite direction to income.

questions.q: Total utility is maximum when marginal utility is ______.
questions.e: TU rises as long as MU is positive, reaches its maximum when MU = 0, and falls when MU turns negative.

questions.q: Goods that are used together, like cars and petrol, are called ______ goods.
questions.e: For complements, a rise in the price of one reduces the demand for the other.

questions.q: When the price of a good falls from ₹10 to ₹8, its quantity demanded rises from 100 to 150 units. Find the price elasticity of demand (percentage method).
For the demand curve q = 100/p (a rectangular hyperbola), what is the price elasticity of demand at every point?
questions.e: Here p × q = 100 always, so total expenditure is constant at every price; such a demand curve has unitary elasticity throughout.

questions.q: Riya has ₹24 to spend on two goods. The price of X is ₹4 and the price of Y is ₹2.
p: (a) What is the maximum quantity of X she can buy?
(b) What is the absolute slope of her budget line (Px/Py)?
(c) At equilibrium, if MU of X is 20 utils, what must the MU of Y be (utils)?
questions.e: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 units of X; slope = Px/Py = 4/2 = 2; equilibrium needs MUx/Px = MUy/Py, so 20/4 = MUy/2, giving MUy = 10.

questions.q: The change in total output from employing one more unit of a variable input is called the ______ product.
questions.e: MP = ΔTP ÷ ΔL; it is the addition to total product from one more unit of the variable input.

questions.q: At 10 units of output, total cost is ₹500 and total fixed cost is ₹200. Find the average variable cost (in ₹).
The total cost of producing 4 units is ₹100 and of 5 units is ₹120. Find the marginal cost of the 5th unit (in ₹).
According to the law of variable proportions, as more units of labour are applied to a fixed amount of land, the marginal product of labour eventually ______.
questions.e: After a point, each extra worker has less of the fixed factor to work with, so MP diminishes.

questions.q: Total product of labour: 1 worker = 10 units, 2 workers = 24 units, 3 workers = 33 units, 4 workers = 40 units.
p: (a) Find the marginal product of the 2nd worker.
(b) Find the average product when 3 workers are employed.
(c) Find the marginal product of the 4th worker.
questions.e: MP2 = 24 − 10 = 14; AP3 = 33 ÷ 3 = 11; MP4 = 40 − 33 = 7, showing diminishing marginal returns after the 2nd worker.

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: Under perfect competition, an individual firm is a price ______.
questions.e: Each firm is too small to influence the market price, so it accepts the price set by the industry.

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: A perfectly competitive firm maximises profit where price equals ______, provided it is rising.
questions.e: Profit is maximum where p = MC and MC is non-decreasing at that output.

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: A firm sells 50 units at a market price of ₹10 each and its total cost is ₹400. Find its profit (in ₹).

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: In the short run, a firm will stop production if the market price falls below the minimum of its ______.
questions.e: If price is below minimum AVC, the firm cannot even cover variable costs, so it shuts down (short-run shut-down point).

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: When the price of a good rises from ₹10 to ₹12, its quantity supplied rises from 100 to 130 units. Find the price elasticity of supply.
questions.e: %ΔQ = 30%; %ΔP = 20%; eS = 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5 (elastic supply).

questions.q: Market equilibrium occurs where market demand equals market ______.
questions.e: At equilibrium, quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, so there is no excess demand or supply.

questions.q: A maximum price fixed by the government below the equilibrium price is called a price ______.
questions.e: A price ceiling, used for essentials like wheat or kerosene, creates excess demand at the controlled price.

questions.q: If both demand and supply increase by the same amount, the equilibrium price ______.
questions.a: remains unchanged|unchanged|remains the same|same|does not change|remains constant|constant
questions.e: An equal rightward shift of both curves raises equilibrium quantity while leaving equilibrium price unchanged.

questions.q: For a commodity, qd = 100 − 2p and qs = 20 + 2p.
p: (a) Find the equilibrium price (₹).
(b) Find the equilibrium quantity (units).
(c) If the government fixes a price ceiling of ₹15, find the excess demand (units).
questions.e: 100 − 2p = 20 + 2p gives p = 20 and q = 60. At ₹15, qd = 70 and qs = 50, so excess demand = 20 units.

questions.q: A variable such as national income, which is measured over a period of time, is a ______ variable.
questions.e: Flows are measured per period (for example per year); stocks, such as capital or wealth, are measured at a point of time.

questions.q: Durable goods such as machines, which help in producing other goods over many years and are not used up in a single year, are called ______ goods.
questions.e: Capital goods are fixed assets of the producer; they wear out gradually over years.

questions.q: The wear and tear of fixed capital during a year is called ______.
questions.e: Depreciation is the fall in the value of fixed capital through normal use; net investment = gross investment − depreciation.

questions.q: In the two-sector circular flow of income, households supply the factors of production to the ______.
questions.e: Households supply land, labour, capital and enterprise to firms and receive rent, wages, interest and profit in return.

questions.q: Gross investment in an economy is ₹500 crore and depreciation is ₹80 crore. Find net investment (in ₹ crore).
questions.e: Net investment = gross investment − depreciation = 500 − 80 = ₹420 crore.

questions.q: GDP at market price is ₹2,000 crore and net indirect taxes are ₹150 crore. Find GDP at factor cost (in ₹ crore).
questions.e: GDPfc = GDPmp − net indirect taxes = 2000 − 150 = ₹1,850 crore.

questions.q: GNP at market price minus depreciation is ______ at market price.
questions.e: NNPmp = GNPmp − depreciation; NDP would be GDP minus depreciation.

questions.q: Real GDP of a country is ₹800 crore and the GDP deflator is 125. Find its nominal GDP (in ₹ crore).
questions.e: GDP deflator = nominal GDP ÷ real GDP × 100, so nominal GDP = 800 × 125 ÷ 100 = ₹1,000 crore.

questions.q: In the expenditure method, GDP = C + I + G + ______, where the last term is exports minus imports.
questions.e: GDP = consumption + investment + government purchases + net exports (X − M).

questions.q: A country's GDP is ₹5,000 crore. Factor income earned by its residents abroad is ₹200 crore and factor income earned by non-residents within the country is ₹300 crore. Find its GNP (in ₹ crore).

Data (₹ crore): private final consumption expenditure 800, government final consumption expenditure 200, gross domestic capital formation 300, net exports −50, depreciation 60, net indirect taxes 90, net factor income from abroad 20.
p: (a) Find GDP at market price (₹ crore).
(b) Find NDP at factor cost (₹ crore).
(c) Find national income (NNP at factor cost, ₹ crore).

questions.q: The direct exchange of goods for goods without the use of money is called the ______ system.
questions.e: Barter exchange needs a double coincidence of wants, which money removes.

questions.q: Barter exchange can take place only when there is a double ______ of wants.
questions.e: Each party must want what the other has to offer; money as a medium of exchange removes this difficulty.

questions.q: Money allows people to hold their wealth and use it in the future. This is the function of money as a ______ of value.
questions.e: Money is a convenient store of value because it can be kept and used later for buying goods and services.

questions.q: The fraction of their deposits that commercial banks must keep as cash reserves with the RBI is called the ______.
questions.e: Raising the CRR reduces the funds banks can lend, so it reduces the money supply.

questions.q: The fraction of their deposits that banks must keep in specified liquid assets, such as government securities, is called the ______.
questions.e: The SLR, along with the CRR, is a tool the RBI uses to control credit.

questions.q: The rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks is the ______ rate.
questions.e: Under reverse repo, banks park surplus funds with the RBI; under repo, banks borrow from the RBI.

questions.q: The buying and selling of government securities by the RBI in the open market to change the money supply is called ______.
questions.e: Open market operations directly change the reserves of commercial banks and hence the money supply.

questions.q: To increase the money supply, the RBI should ______ government securities in the open market.
questions.e: When the RBI buys securities it pays money to the sellers, increasing bank reserves and hence the money supply.

questions.q: If the reserve ratio that banks must keep is 10%, what is the value of the money multiplier?
questions.e: Money multiplier = 1 ÷ reserve ratio = 1 ÷ 0.1 = 10.

questions.q: Currency notes and coins that have no intrinsic value and are accepted because the government declares them legal tender are called ______ money.
questions.e: Fiat money derives its value from the authority of the government, not from the material it is made of.

questions.q: The legal reserve ratio is 25% and a new deposit of ₹2,000 is made in the banking system.
p: (a) Find the money multiplier.
(b) Find the total deposits that can be created (₹).
(c) If the reserve ratio is cut to 20%, find the total deposits that can be created (₹).
questions.e: Multiplier = 1 ÷ 0.25 = 4, so deposits = 2000 × 4 = ₹8,000; at 20% the multiplier is 5, giving 2000 × 5 = ₹10,000.

questions.q: The ratio of total consumption to total income is called the ______.
questions.e: APC = C ÷ Y; it can be more than 1 at low incomes because of autonomous consumption.

questions.q: What is the sum of the marginal propensity to consume and the marginal propensity to save?
questions.e: Every extra rupee of income is either consumed or saved, so MPC + MPS = 1.

questions.q: Investment that does not depend on the level of income is called ______ investment.
questions.e: In the short-run model, planned investment is taken as autonomous, so the investment curve is a horizontal line.

questions.q: When aggregate demand falls short of aggregate supply at the full employment level of output, the shortfall is called the ______ gap.
questions.e: Deficient demand leads to falling output and employment; the shortfall is the deflationary gap.

questions.q: If the marginal propensity to save is 0.2, what is the value of the investment multiplier?
Planned or intended values of economic variables, as distinct from their actual values, are called ______ values.
questions.e: Ex ante means planned; ex post means actual or realised.

questions.q: In an economy, the consumption function is C = 40 + 0.8Y. Find consumption (in ₹ crore) when income is ₹500 crore.
The consumption function is C = 40 + 0.8Y and autonomous investment is ₹60 crore. Find the equilibrium level of income (in ₹ crore).
If the investment multiplier is 4, what is the marginal propensity to consume?
questions.e: k = 1 ÷ (1 − MPC), so 4 = 1 ÷ (1 − MPC), giving 1 − MPC = 0.25 and MPC = 0.75.

questions.q: An economy has the consumption function C = 100 + 0.6Y and autonomous investment of ₹100 crore.
p: (a) Find the equilibrium income (₹ crore).
(b) Find consumption at equilibrium income (₹ crore).
(c) Find saving at equilibrium income (₹ crore).
questions.e: Y = 100 + 0.6Y + 100 gives 0.4Y = 200, so Y = 500; C = 100 + 0.6 × 500 = 400; S = 500 − 400 = 100, which equals investment at equilibrium.

questions.q: A budget in which the government's estimated receipts are equal to its estimated expenditure is a ______ budget.
questions.e: If receipts exceed expenditure the budget is in surplus; if expenditure exceeds receipts it is in deficit.

questions.q: A tax such as the goods and services tax (GST), whose burden can be shifted to others, is an ______ tax.
questions.e: Indirect taxes are levied on goods and services and are passed on to buyers through higher prices.

questions.q: Receipts that neither create a liability nor reduce the assets of the government, such as taxes, are ______ receipts.
questions.e: Revenue receipts consist of tax revenue and non-tax revenue such as interest, dividends and fees.

questions.q: Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − ______.
questions.e: A revenue deficit means the government is dissaving: its current receipts do not cover its current expenditure.

questions.q: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − ______.
questions.e: The primary deficit shows the borrowing needed for current spending other than interest on past debt.

questions.q: The recovery of loans earlier given by the government is a ______ receipt.
questions.e: Recovery of loans reduces the government's financial assets, so it is a non-debt capital receipt.

questions.q: The fiscal deficit of a government is ₹900 crore and its interest payments are ₹400 crore. Find the primary deficit (in ₹ crore).
questions.e: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments = 900 − 400 = ₹500 crore.

questions.q: Revenue expenditure of a government is ₹1,500 crore and its revenue receipts are ₹1,200 crore. Find the revenue deficit (in ₹ crore).
questions.e: Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts = 1500 − 1200 = ₹300 crore.

questions.q: If the primary deficit is zero, the fiscal deficit is equal to ______.
questions.e: Since primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments, a zero primary deficit means borrowing is needed only to pay interest.

questions.q: Budget data (₹ crore): tax revenue 800, non-tax revenue 200, revenue expenditure 1,100 (including interest payments 150), capital expenditure 400, recovery of loans 50, disinvestment 50, borrowings 400.
p: (a) Find the revenue deficit (₹ crore).
(b) Find the fiscal deficit (₹ crore).
(c) Find the primary deficit (₹ crore).

questions.q: The difference between the value of exports of goods and the value of imports of goods is the balance of ______.
questions.e: The balance of trade covers only goods (visibles); the current account also includes services and transfers.

questions.q: The price of one currency in terms of another currency is the foreign ______ rate.
questions.e: For example, if ₹84 buy one US dollar, the exchange rate is ₹84 per dollar.

questions.q: Trade in services such as shipping, banking and tourism, along with transfers, is recorded as ______ in the current account.
questions.e: Services, income and transfers are invisibles because they are not seen crossing borders, unlike goods.

questions.q: Foreign direct investment and portfolio investment are recorded in the ______ account of the balance of payments.
questions.e: The capital account records international purchases and sales of assets such as shares, bonds and land, and borrowing.

questions.q: Under a fixed exchange rate system, a reduction in the value of the domestic currency by the government is called ______.
questions.e: Devaluation is a deliberate policy act under a fixed rate; depreciation happens through market forces under a flexible rate.

questions.q: A system in which the exchange rate is largely set by the market but the central bank intervenes to limit fluctuations is called managed ______.
questions.e: Managed floating, also called dirty floating, is a mix of the flexible and fixed systems.

questions.q: Under a flexible exchange rate, the price of one US dollar falls from ₹84 to ₹80. The Indian rupee has ______.
questions.e: Fewer rupees are now needed to buy a dollar, so the rupee has gained value (appreciated).

questions.q: Balance of payments transactions undertaken for their own sake, such as for profit, and not to bridge a BoP gap are called ______ transactions.
questions.e: Autonomous transactions are above the line; a BoP surplus or deficit is the balance of autonomous transactions.

questions.q: Transactions made to cover a deficit or surplus in the balance of payments, such as changes in official reserves, are called ______ transactions.
questions.e: Accommodating transactions are below the line and are made to settle the BoP gap.

questions.q: If the rupee depreciates against the US dollar, Indian goods become ______ for buyers in the USA.
questions.e: A dollar now buys more rupees, so Indian goods cost fewer dollars and exports tend to rise.

questions.q: A country has a current account deficit of ₹300 crore and a capital account surplus of ₹250 crore (autonomous transactions only). By how much must its official reserves fall to settle the balance of payments (in ₹ crore)?
questions.e: Overall BoP deficit = −300 + 250 = −50, so official reserves must be drawn down by ₹50 crore.

questions.q: Under a flexible exchange rate, the demand for dollars is D = 1000 − 10e and the supply of dollars is S = 200 + 10e, where e is the number of rupees per dollar.
p: (a) Find the equilibrium exchange rate (₹ per dollar).
(b) Find the equilibrium quantity of dollars traded.
(c) If the demand for dollars rises, does the rupee appreciate or depreciate?
depreciate|depreciates|depreciation
questions.e: 1000 − 10e = 200 + 10e gives e = 40 and quantity = 1000 − 400 = 600; higher demand for dollars raises e, so the rupee depreciates.

questions.q: The study of the behaviour of individual economic agents, such as a consumer or a firm, is called ______.
questions.e: Microeconomics studies individual markets and agents; macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole.

questions.q: The value of the next best alternative that has to be given up when a choice is made is called ______ cost.
questions.e: Because resources have alternative uses, every choice has an opportunity cost.

questions.q: Deciding who gets the goods and services produced in an economy is the central problem of 'for ______ to produce'.
questions.e: The three central problems are what, how and for whom to produce.

questions.q: Economic analysis that deals with what ought to be, and involves value judgements, is called ______ economics.
questions.e: Normative economics judges whether outcomes are desirable; positive economics describes how things actually work.

questions.q: Economic analysis that studies how the economy actually works, without value judgements, is called ______ economics.
questions.e: Positive statements can be tested against facts.

questions.q: An economy in which the government or a central authority decides what, how and for whom to produce is a centrally ______ economy.
questions.e: In a centrally planned economy, the central authority plans all important economic activities.

questions.q: An economy in which economic activities are organised through the free interaction of buyers and sellers is a ______ economy.
questions.e: In a market economy, prices determined by demand and supply guide the decisions of buyers and sellers.

questions.q: Choosing between labour-intensive and capital-intensive techniques of production is the central problem of '______ to produce'.
questions.e: The problem of how to produce is about which combination of resources and technique to use.

questions.q: A point inside the production possibility curve shows that the economy's resources are ______.
questions.e: If some resources are idle or used inefficiently, the economy produces at a point below the PPC.

questions.q: The production possibility curve is concave to the origin because the marginal opportunity cost ______ as more of one good is produced.
questions.e: Resources are not equally efficient in all uses, so ever more of one good must be given up for each extra unit of the other.

questions.q: With the given resources and technology, a point outside the production possibility curve is ______.
questions.e: Such a point can be reached only if resources increase or technology improves, shifting the PPC outward.

questions.q: If an economy's production possibility curve is a downward-sloping straight line, its marginal opportunity cost is ______.
questions.e: A straight line has the same slope throughout, so the marginal rate of transformation is constant.

questions.q: An economy produces wheat and cloth. Its production possibilities (wheat, cloth) are (0, 50), (1, 48), (2, 44), (3, 38) and (4, 30).
p: (a) How many units of cloth must be given up to produce the 3rd unit of wheat?
(b) How many units of cloth must be given up to produce the 4th unit of wheat?
(c) Is the marginal opportunity cost of wheat increasing, decreasing or constant?
increasing|rising|increases
questions.e: Cloth given up: 2, 4, 6, 8 for the 1st to 4th units of wheat (44 − 38 = 6; 38 − 30 = 8), so the marginal opportunity cost is increasing and the PPC is concave.

questions.q: According to the law of diminishing marginal utility, the marginal utility from successive units of a good ______ as more of it is consumed.
questions.e: Each extra unit adds less satisfaction than the previous one.

questions.q: A curve joining all the bundles of two goods that give a consumer the same level of satisfaction is an ______ curve.
questions.e: The consumer is indifferent between all bundles on one indifference curve.

questions.q: The rate at which a consumer is willing to substitute one good for another while remaining on the same indifference curve is the marginal rate of ______.
questions.e: MRS is the absolute slope of the indifference curve; it diminishes along a convex indifference curve.

questions.q: A change in the quantity demanded caused by a change in the good's own price is shown by a ______ along the demand curve.
questions.e: Changes in other factors, such as income or prices of related goods, shift the demand curve instead.

questions.q: Two goods for which a rise in the price of one raises the demand for the other, like tea and coffee, are called ______.
questions.e: When tea becomes dearer, people switch to coffee, so the demand for coffee rises.

questions.q: When the price of a good falls, the total expenditure on it rises. The demand for the good is ______.
questions.e: Under the total expenditure method, expenditure moving opposite to price shows elastic demand (eD > 1).

questions.q: When the price of a good rises from ₹5 to ₹6, its quantity demanded falls from 40 to 36 units. Find the price elasticity of demand (percentage method).
A consumer has an income of ₹100. The price of good X is ₹4 and of good Y is ₹5. If she buys 10 units of X, what is the maximum number of units of Y she can buy?
questions.e: Budget line: 4x + 5y = 100; with x = 10, 5y = 60, so y = 12.

questions.q: A consumer spends her income on a single good. In utility analysis she is in equilibrium when the marginal utility of the good, measured in rupees, equals its ______.
questions.e: She keeps buying while MU (in rupees) exceeds the price and stops where MU = price.

questions.q: Costs that do not change with the level of output, such as the rent of a factory building, are ______ costs.
questions.e: Fixed costs must be paid even when output is zero.

questions.q: Total product divided by the number of units of the variable input gives the ______ product.
questions.e: AP = TP ÷ L.

questions.q: The period in which at least one factor of production cannot be varied is called the ______ run.
questions.e: In the long run, all factors of production can be varied.

questions.q: The relationship between the inputs used and the maximum output that can be produced from them is called the ______ function.
questions.e: A production function such as q = f(L, K) gives the maximum output for each combination of inputs.

questions.q: As output increases, average fixed cost ______ continuously.
questions.e: AFC = TFC ÷ q; a fixed total is spread over more units, so the AFC curve is a rectangular hyperbola.

questions.q: Total fixed cost of a firm is ₹600. Find the average fixed cost at an output of 20 units (in ₹).
When marginal product is greater than average product, the average product ______.
questions.e: If the extra unit adds more than the average, it pulls the average up.

questions.q: The marginal cost curve cuts the average variable cost curve at the ______ point of the AVC curve.
questions.e: AVC falls while MC is below it and rises when MC is above it, so MC passes through the minimum of AVC.

questions.q: When total product is at its maximum, what is the marginal product?
questions.e: TP rises while MP is positive, is maximum when MP = 0, and falls when MP becomes negative.

questions.q: At 4 units of output, total variable cost is ₹160 and total fixed cost is ₹40. Find the average total cost (in ₹).
A firm's total fixed cost is ₹60. Its total variable cost is ₹40 for 1 unit, ₹70 for 2 units and ₹120 for 3 units.
p: (a) Find the total cost of producing 3 units (₹).
(b) Find the marginal cost of the 3rd unit (₹).
(c) Find the average variable cost at 2 units (₹).

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: Revenue per unit of output sold is called ______ revenue.
questions.e: AR = TR ÷ q; under perfect competition AR equals the market price.

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: Total revenue = price × ______.
questions.e: TR is the money a firm receives from selling its output: TR = p × q.

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: A table showing the quantities of a good that a firm is willing to sell at different prices is a supply ______.
questions.e: The supply curve is the graphical form of the supply schedule.

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: For a firm under perfect competition, marginal revenue is always equal to ______.
questions.e: The firm can sell any quantity at the market price, so each extra unit adds exactly the price to TR: MR = AR = p.

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: A firm's total revenue from selling 10 units is ₹200 and from selling 11 units is ₹220. Find the marginal revenue of the 11th unit (in ₹).

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: A rise in the prices of inputs, other things remaining the same, shifts a firm's supply curve to the ______.
questions.e: Higher input prices raise the firm's marginal cost, so it supplies less at every price.

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: What is the price elasticity of supply of a vertical straight-line supply curve?
questions.e: Quantity supplied does not change whatever the price, so supply is perfectly inelastic (eS = 0).

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: What is the price elasticity of supply of a straight-line supply curve that passes through the origin?
questions.e: Along such a line q is proportional to p, so %Δq always equals %Δp and eS = 1.

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: The market price is ₹12. A perfectly competitive firm produces 40 units at an average cost of ₹10. Find its total profit (in ₹).

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: When the price of a good rises from ₹20 to ₹25, its quantity supplied rises from 200 to 220 units. Find the price elasticity of supply.

questions.t: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.q: A perfectly competitive firm faces a market price of ₹10. Its total cost (₹) is 5 at 0 units, 12 at 1 unit, 17 at 2 units, 24 at 3 units, 33 at 4 units and 46 at 5 units.
p: (a) What is its total fixed cost (₹)?
(b) At what output is its profit maximum (units)?
(c) What is the maximum profit (₹)?
questions.e: TFC = TC at zero output = 5. Profits (TR − TC) for 1 to 5 units are −2, 3, 6, 7 and 4, so profit is highest (₹7) at 4 units, where MC (9) ≤ price and the next unit's MC (13) exceeds it.

questions.q: When the quantity demanded is greater than the quantity supplied at a given price, there is excess ______.
questions.e: Excess demand pushes the price up towards equilibrium.

questions.q: The price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied is called the ______ price.
questions.e: At the equilibrium price the plans of buyers and sellers match.

questions.q: If there is excess supply at the current price, the price tends to ______.
questions.e: Sellers who cannot sell all they want cut prices until excess supply disappears.

questions.q: When demand increases and supply remains unchanged, the equilibrium quantity ______.
questions.e: A rightward shift of the demand curve raises both equilibrium price and equilibrium quantity.

questions.q: When supply increases and demand remains unchanged, the equilibrium price ______.
questions.e: A rightward shift of the supply curve lowers the equilibrium price and raises the equilibrium quantity.

questions.q: A government-fixed minimum support price for wheat, set above the equilibrium price, is an example of a price ______.
questions.e: A price floor is a minimum price; agricultural price support and the minimum wage are examples.

questions.q: When a price ceiling is fixed below the equilibrium price, the government often distributes the good through ______ shops using ration cards.
questions.e: The ceiling creates excess demand, so the limited supply is rationed; black marketing may also arise.

questions.q: For a commodity, qd = 150 − 5p and qs = 30 + 3p. Find the equilibrium price (in ₹).
questions.e: 150 − 5p = 30 + 3p gives 8p = 120, so p = ₹15 (and q = 75 units).

questions.q: If both demand and supply decrease by the same amount, the equilibrium quantity ______.
questions.e: Equal leftward shifts of both curves leave the price unchanged but reduce the equilibrium quantity.

questions.q: If demand increases and supply decreases at the same time, the equilibrium price ______.
questions.e: Both changes push the price up; the effect on quantity depends on the sizes of the two shifts.

questions.q: A price floor fixed above the equilibrium price leads to excess ______.
questions.e: At the higher price, sellers offer more and buyers want less, so a surplus appears.

questions.q: For a commodity, qd = 100 − 3p and qs = 2p − 10.
p: (a) Find the equilibrium price (₹).
(b) Find the equilibrium quantity (units).
(c) If the government fixes a price floor of ₹25, find the excess supply (units).
questions.e: 100 − 3p = 2p − 10 gives p = 22 and q = 34. At ₹25, qd = 25 and qs = 40, so excess supply = 15 units.

questions.q: The body set up in 1950, with the Prime Minister as its Chairperson, to formulate India's Five Year Plans was the ______.
questions.e: The Planning Commission was set up in 1950 with the Prime Minister as Chairperson, and the era of Five Year Plans began in 1951.

questions.q: A long-term plan covering a period of about 20 years, which provides the basis for the Five Year Plans, is called a ______ plan.
questions.e: Each Five Year Plan works towards the long-term goals of a perspective plan.

questions.q: India chose an economic system combining features of capitalism and socialism, with both a public and a private sector. Such an economy is called a ______ economy.
questions.e: In a mixed economy the market supplies most goods, while the government plays a key role in planning and in strategic sectors.

questions.q: The planning goal of avoiding imports of goods, especially food, that could be produced in India itself is called ______.
questions.e: Self-reliance aimed to reduce dependence on foreign countries, particularly for food.

questions.q: Adopting new technology in production and changing social outlook, such as recognising that women should have the same rights as men, were part of which goal of planning?
questions.e: Modernisation meant both the adoption of new technology and changes in social outlook.

questions.q: Fixing the maximum size of land that an individual can own, as a land reform measure, is called a land ______.
questions.e: Land ceilings aimed to reduce the concentration of land ownership in a few hands.

questions.q: In the first phase of the Green Revolution, the use of HYV seeds mainly benefited the regions growing which crop?
questions.e: In its first phase (about mid-1960s to mid-1970s), HYV seeds were used mainly in the more affluent states and primarily benefited wheat-growing regions.

questions.q: The portion of agricultural produce that farmers sell in the market is called the ______ surplus.
questions.e: The Green Revolution raised output enough for farmers to sell a larger marketed surplus, which helped keep foodgrain prices down.

questions.q: The Village and Small-Scale Industries Committee of 1955, which noted the possibility of using small-scale industries for promoting rural development, is also called the ______ Committee.
questions.e: The Karve Committee saw small-scale industry as a way to generate rural employment because it is more labour-intensive.

questions.q: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, a private firm needed a ______ from the government to start a new industry or to expand output.
questions.e: Industrial licensing was used to promote industry in backward regions and to control the expansion of private industry.

questions.q: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, industries in the first category were to be exclusively owned by the ______.
questions.e: The first category was reserved for the state; in the second the private sector could supplement the state; the third was left to the private sector.

questions.q: Reform measures that remove restrictions on economic activities and open up various sectors of the economy are called ______.
questions.e: Liberalisation removed many controls, such as industrial licensing, that had been placed on the economy before 1991.

questions.q: The integration of the economy of a country with the world economy is called ______.
questions.e: Globalisation creates greater interdependence and integration through trade, investment and the flow of technology.

questions.q: To meet the 1991 crisis, India borrowed from the World Bank and the ______.
questions.e: India received loans from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund and agreed to introduce the New Economic Policy.

questions.q: As an immediate measure to resolve the 1991 balance of payments crisis, the government reduced the value of the rupee against foreign currencies. This is called ______.
questions.e: Devaluation of the rupee made exports cheaper and helped increase the inflow of foreign exchange.

questions.q: In which year was the Goods and Services Tax (GST), a unified indirect tax system, introduced in India?
questions.e: GST was introduced in July 2017, replacing many indirect taxes with one tax ("One Nation, One Tax, One Market").

questions.q: On 8 November 2016, the government announced that the existing ₹500 and ₹1,000 currency notes would no longer be legal tender. This step is known as ______.
questions.e: Demonetisation aimed to tackle corruption, black money, terrorism and the circulation of fake currency.

questions.q: To improve efficiency, the government gave certain public sector enterprises greater managerial autonomy by granting them the status of Maharatnas, Navratnas and ______.
questions.e: Such status gives profit-making public sector enterprises more freedom in taking financial and managerial decisions.

questions.q: Abolishing industrial licensing for almost all product categories in 1991 was a measure of which policy: liberalisation, privatisation or globalisation?
questions.e: Deregulation of the industrial sector, including the abolition of most licensing, was part of liberalisation.

questions.q: One of the major aims of the financial sector reforms is to change the role of the RBI from a regulator to a ______ of the financial sector.
questions.e: Under the reforms, the financial sector was allowed to take decisions on many matters without consulting the RBI.

questions.q: Merchant bankers, mutual funds and pension funds from abroad that are allowed to invest in Indian financial markets are known by the abbreviation ______.
questions.e: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were allowed to invest in Indian financial markets as part of the financial sector reforms.

questions.q: Reforms in the government's taxation and public expenditure policies are reforms in its ______ policy.
questions.e: Taxation and public expenditure policies are collectively known as fiscal policy.

questions.q: Answer the following about the economic reforms of 1991.
p: (a) The 1991 crisis arose because India's ______ exchange reserves fell too low to pay for imports for more than about two weeks.
foreign
(b) Transferring the ownership or management of a government enterprise to the private sector is called ______.
privatisation|privatization
(c) Give the abbreviation for business process outsourcing, such as call centres and medical transcription.
bpo|bpos
questions.e: The foreign exchange crisis led to the New Economic Policy; privatisation reduced the government's role in enterprises; globalisation boosted BPO services in India.

questions.q: The stock of skill and expertise of a nation at a particular point of time is called its ______ capital.
questions.e: Human capital is built through education, health, on-the-job training, migration and information.

questions.q: The process of adding to the stock of skill and expertise of a nation over time is called human capital ______.
questions.e: Human capital formation turns people into productive resources, much as physical capital formation adds machines and buildings.

questions.q: Spending to acquire ______ about the labour market, such as wages and job openings, is a source of human capital formation.
questions.e: Such information helps people choose the right jobs and courses, so making better use of their human capital.

questions.q: The body that regulates technical education in India is the ______.
questions.a: aicte|all india council for technical education
questions.e: The AICTE regulates technical education, while the UGC regulates university education.

questions.q: The body that regulates medical research in India is the ______.
questions.e: The ICMR, along with the health ministries, regulates the health sector.

questions.q: The Right to Education Act, 2009 made free education a fundamental right of all children aged 6 to ______ years.
questions.e: The RTE Act, 2009 provides for free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.

questions.q: The Education Commission (1964–66) recommended spending at least what percentage of GDP on education?
questions.e: The Education Commission recommended that at least 6% of GDP be spent on education.

questions.q: Human capital treats education and health as a means to raise labour productivity, whereas human ______ treats them as integral to human well-being.
questions.e: Human development sees education and health as ends in themselves, whether or not they raise productivity.

questions.q: Spending on education by individuals is similar to spending on capital goods by companies: both aim to increase future ______ over a period of time.
questions.e: Education raises a person's future earning capacity, just as investment raises a firm's future profits.

questions.q: Higher human capital raises growth, and higher growth raises incomes that can be spent on education and health. So the causality between human capital and economic growth flows in ______ direction.
questions.e: NCERT notes that the causality between human capital and economic growth flows in either direction.

questions.q: An educated person who spreads awareness of hygiene in her community benefits not only herself but also society. Such a benefit to society is called an ______ benefit.
questions.e: Human capital creates external benefits, so it benefits society as well as its owner.

questions.q: Physical capital depreciates through wear and tear, whereas human capital depreciates mainly through ______.
questions.e: Depreciation of human capital with ageing can be reduced through continuous investment in education and health.

questions.q: Because human capital is embodied in its owner, the market can only sell the ______ of human capital, not the capital itself.
questions.e: A doctor can sell medical services, but the doctor's skills cannot be separated from the doctor and sold.

questions.q: Growing fruits, vegetables, flowers and medicinal plants is called ______.
questions.e: Horticulture improves food and nutrition and provides employment and income to rural families.

questions.q: Institutional credit to rural areas expanded rapidly after the nationalisation of commercial banks in which year?
questions.e: After bank nationalisation in 1969, India adopted social banking and a multi-agency approach to meet rural credit needs.

questions.q: The period 1991–2003, in which planned investment in horticulture became highly productive, is called the ______ Revolution.
questions.e: Rapid growth in horticulture output made the sector a sustainable source of employment and income.

questions.q: A shift in cropping pattern and a shift of workers from agriculture to allied activities and non-farm sectors are together called agricultural ______.
questions.e: Diversification reduces the risk of depending only on crops and provides productive jobs to the rural population.

questions.q: Farmers' markets in Andhra Pradesh where farmers sell vegetables and fruits directly to consumers are called ______.
questions.e: Rythu Bazars are an alternative marketing channel that cuts out middlemen.

questions.q: To ensure a fair price for farmers, the government fixes a ______ price for certain agricultural products.
questions.e: The minimum support price (MSP) protects farmers against a fall in prices of their produce.

questions.q: Stocks of wheat and rice kept by the government to meet shortages and to supply the public distribution system are called ______ stocks.
questions.e: Buffer stocks help stabilise foodgrain supplies and prices.

questions.q: Farmers in Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan sell their produce directly to consumers in markets called ______.
questions.e: Apni Mandi is an alternative marketing channel that raises farmers' share in the price paid by consumers.

questions.q: Commercial banks, regional rural banks and cooperatives are institutional sources of rural credit, whereas moneylenders and traders are ______ sources.
questions.e: Non-institutional lenders often charged very high interest rates, which trapped small farmers in debt.

questions.q: Because rural credit in India is supplied by commercial banks, regional rural banks, cooperatives and land development banks together, the system follows a ______ approach.
questions.e: After 1969, a multi-agency approach was adopted to provide adequate institutional credit in rural areas.

questions.q: The public body that procures foodgrains and maintains buffer stocks of wheat and rice in India is the ______.
questions.e: The Food Corporation of India keeps buffer stocks and supplies foodgrains to the public distribution system.

questions.q: All those who are engaged in economic activities, in whatever capacity, high or low, are called ______.
questions.e: Workers contribute to the gross domestic product through their economic activities.

questions.q: The percentage of the population that is working is called the worker-______ ratio.
questions.e: Worker-population ratio = (total number of workers ÷ total population) × 100.

questions.q: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 promises how many days of guaranteed wage employment in a year to rural households that volunteer for unskilled manual work?
questions.e: MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a year to every rural household that volunteers for unskilled manual work.

questions.q: All public sector establishments, and private sector establishments that employ at least how many hired workers, are called formal sector establishments?
questions.e: Formal sector establishments are public sector establishments and private establishments employing 10 or more hired workers.

questions.q: Farm workers who find no work during certain months of the year because of the agricultural cycle face ______ unemployment.
questions.e: Seasonal unemployment is common in rural India, where farm work is available only in certain seasons.

questions.q: A situation in which the economy produces more goods and services but without generating a matching growth in employment is called ______ growth.
questions.e: Jobless growth means GDP rises faster than employment opportunities.

questions.q: The shift of workers from self-employment and regular salaried jobs to casual wage work is called ______ of the workforce.
questions.e: Casualisation leaves workers without job security or social security benefits.

questions.q: According to NCERT, the largest share of India's workforce is employed in the ______ sector.
questions.e: Most of India's workforce, especially in rural areas, depends on the primary sector, mainly agriculture.

questions.q: Over the years, the share of workers in the informal sector has risen while the share in the formal sector has fallen. This process is called ______ of the workforce.
questions.e: Informal sector workers do not get regular income or social security benefits.

questions.q: According to NCERT, the worker-population ratio in India is higher in ______ areas than in urban areas.
questions.e: In rural areas many people, including women, take part in farm and other work because incomes are low and education levels are limited.

questions.q: A factory worker who is able and willing to work but does not find any work at all is in ______ unemployment.
questions.e: Open unemployment, mostly found in urban areas, is visible because the person has no work at all.

questions.q: Resources such as trees in forests and fish in the ocean, which can be used without the possibility of being exhausted, are ______ resources.
questions.e: Renewable resources keep regenerating, so they are not used up as long as use stays within the rate of regeneration.

questions.q: Coal and petroleum get exhausted with extraction and use. They are ______ resources.
questions.e: Non-renewable resources such as fossil fuels have a fixed stock that is used up over time.

questions.q: Scenery and natural beauty are examples of the ______ services provided by the environment.
questions.e: The environment supplies resources, assimilates waste, sustains life and provides aesthetic services such as scenery.

questions.q: Global warming is mainly caused by the increase in ______ gases, such as carbon dioxide and methane, in the atmosphere.
questions.e: Greenhouse gases trap heat, raising the average temperature of the earth's lower atmosphere.

questions.q: The ozone layer is depleted mainly by chlorine compounds called ______, used in refrigerators, air-conditioners and aerosol sprays.
questions.e: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and halons release chlorine and bromine that break down stratospheric ozone.

questions.q: The ozone layer in the stratosphere protects life on the earth from harmful ______ radiation.
questions.e: Ozone depletion lets more ultraviolet radiation reach the earth, causing skin cancer and harm to crops and aquatic life.

questions.q: In rural areas, the use of ______ as cooking fuel in place of firewood and dung cakes reduces air pollution and deforestation.
questions.e: Cleaner fuels like LPG and gobar gas (biogas) cut indoor pollution and save forests.

questions.q: In Delhi, the use of ______ as fuel in public transport has helped lower air pollution.
questions.e: Switching public transport to CNG reduced vehicle emissions in Delhi.

questions.q: Solar energy can be converted directly into electricity with the help of ______ cells.
questions.e: Photovoltaic cells allow clean electricity to be generated from sunlight, a renewable source.

questions.q: In mountainous regions, streams can be used to generate electricity locally through small, environment-friendly ______ plants.
questions.e: Mini-hydel plants are environment-friendly, need no large dams and can meet local electricity needs.

questions.q: The environment can perform its functions without interruption only when resource extraction does not exceed regeneration and wastes stay within its assimilating ability. This limit is called its ______ capacity.
questions.e: When demand on the environment exceeds its carrying capacity, an environmental crisis results.

questions.q: Answer the following about global environmental issues.
p: (a) The gradual increase in the average temperature of the earth's lower atmosphere is called global ______.
warming
(b) The 1997 United Nations agreement to reduce greenhouse gas emissions is named after which city in Japan?
kyoto
(c) Name the body set up in India in 1974 to monitor air and water quality and control pollution.
cpcb|central pollution control board
questions.e: Global warming results from rising greenhouse gases; the Kyoto Protocol (1997) set targets to cut emissions; the Central Pollution Control Board was set up in 1974.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: In which year was the People's Republic of China established?
questions.e: The People's Republic of China was established in 1949 under one-party rule, two years after India's independence.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: In which year did Pakistan announce its first Five Year Plan, now called the Medium Term Development Plan?
questions.e: India's First Plan covered 1951–56, China announced its first plan in 1953 and Pakistan in 1956.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: The Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution in China were launched under the leadership of ______.
questions.a: mao|mao zedong|mao tse-tung|mao tse tung|chairman mao
questions.e: Mao led China until the 1970s; the reforms of 1978 came after his period.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: In which year did China announce its First Five Year Plan?
questions.e: China announced its first Five Year Plan in 1953, India in 1951 and Pakistan in 1956.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: In 1965, Mao introduced the Great Proletarian ______ Revolution, under which students and professionals were sent to work and learn in the countryside.
questions.e: The Cultural Revolution lasted from 1966 to 1976.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: The system in China under which people collectively cultivated the land was called the ______ system.
questions.e: By 1958 there were about 26,000 communes covering almost all of China's farm population.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: To control population growth, China introduced the ______ norm in the late 1970s.
questions.e: The one-child norm slowed population growth but also lowered the sex ratio and will raise the proportion of elderly people.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: In the first phase of China's reforms, commune lands were divided into small plots and allocated, for use but not ownership, to individual ______.
questions.e: Allocating plots to households raised farm output and incomes in the early reform years.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: Pakistan nationalised capital goods industries in the 1970s, but in the late 1970s and 1980s the thrust of its policy shifted to ______ and encouragement of the private sector.
questions.e: Pakistan moved from nationalisation in the 1970s to denationalisation in the 1980s, before formal reforms in 1988.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: In China's reforms, farmers and industrial units sold fixed quantities of inputs and outputs at government-fixed prices and the rest at market prices. This system is called ______ pricing.
questions.e: Dual pricing let market prices operate gradually as output increased.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: Among India, China and Pakistan, which country has the highest population density?
questions.e: China has the largest area, so its population density is the lowest of the three; India's is the highest.

questions.t: Comparative Development Experiences of India and its Neighbours
questions.q: Among India, China and Pakistan, which country performs best on human development indicators such as the Human Development Index and life expectancy?
questions.e: China is ahead of India and Pakistan on most human development indicators.
